title: Understanding Rotational Kinetic Energy
text: Rotational kinetic energy is given by the formula $$KE_{\text{rot}}=\frac{1}{2}I\omega**{2}$$, $$where$$ $$I$$ is the moment of inertia and $$\omega$$ is the angular velocity.

title: Calculate the Moment of Inertia
text: The moment of inertia $$I$$ for a uniform cylindrical object is calculated using the formula $$I=\frac{1}{2}MR**{2}$$.

title: Calculate $$I$$
text: Given that the mass $$M$$ is $$10\, \text{kg}$$ and the radius $$R$$ is $$12\, \text{cm}$$ (or $$0.12\, \text{m}\$\$)$$, $$calculate$$ $$the$$ $$moment$$ $$of$$ $$inertia$$ $$I$$.

title: Convert Angular Velocity
text: Convert the angular velocity from revolutions per minute $$\frac{rev}{min}$$ to radians per second $$\frac{rad}{s}$$. Use the conversion: $$1\text{rev}=2\pi\text{rad}$$ and $$1\text{min}=60\text{s}$$.

title: Calculate Rotational Kinetic Energy
text: Now that you have $$I=0.072$$ $$kg m^2$$ and $$\omega=157.08\, \tfrac{\text{rad}}{\text{s}}$$, $$calculate$$ $$the$$ $$rotational$$ $$kinetic$$ $$energy$$ $$using$$ $$KE_{\text{rot}}=\frac{1}{2}I\omega**{2}$$.
